title: Digital reach, AI use, civic attention, and institutional scrutiny remain separate control surfaces
source_unit: Bounded cross-source comparison of Pew adult and teen surveys, Pew news/civic analysis, and an FTC information-gathering inquiry; units are preserved rather than pooled

observations.period: 2025; adult platform reach and daily frequency

denominator.unit: US adults in Pew/SSRS survey; frequency comparison uses a separate Pew adult survey

observations.method: Pew adult social-media survey comparison; estimates are self-reported reach or frequency and come from separate question universes where noted.
observations.uncertainty: Reach and frequency do not measure content, recommendation exposure, persuasion, spending, dependence, privacy loss, or ability to leave. Platform estimates are not a common attention index.
observations.subgroup: US adults, with platform-specific age and demographic differences in the source record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Broad reach can reflect useful, replaceable, or brief use and does not by itself imply concentrated control over users.

denominator.unit: US teens ages 13-17 in completed Pew/Ipsos KnowledgePanel dyads

almost_constant_platform_use.unit: percent using at least one of five measured platforms almost constantly

observations.method: Pew/Ipsos survey of US teens; platform and chatbot estimates use question-specific valid response universes.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not identify whether use is school-mediated, socially necessary, beneficial, harmful, monitored, monetized, or difficult to stop. It does not follow exit attempts or later outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Teens ages 13-17, with age, income, and race/ethnicity differences in chatbot use reported separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: High teen use can be instrumental, socially useful, and reversible; lower use can reflect access constraints rather than autonomy.

observations.period: February 17-23, 2026; adult chatbot use, purpose, privacy, and governance concern

denominator.unit: US adult survey respondents; work-use items use an employed-adult universe

observations.method: Pew nationally representative survey of US adults; self-reported chatbot use, purposes, expectations, and regulatory confidence.
observations.uncertainty: Reported use is not telemetry, reliance, accuracy, dependence, actual privacy loss, or observed regulatory performance. Purpose categories may overlap.
observations.subgroup: US adults, with work-task, age, and other subgroup estimates in the source record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Practical usefulness and concern can coexist; concern about privacy or pace does not prove a particular product caused loss of control.

observations.period: 2025; news-source ecosystems, influencer exposure, and civic-action typology

denominator.unit: US adult survey respondents for news-source items; other results use published subgroup percentages

connectors.unit: percent of US adults in published engagement typology

mobilizers.unit: percent of US adults in published engagement typology

observations.method: Pew survey and typology combining news, political, civic, religious, and attention measures; source ecosystems and civic actions are described separately.
observations.uncertainty: Influencer exposure, source trust, civic style, and voting/contacting officials are not a causal sequence. Prior identity, resources, organizations, and offline institutions may explain observed differences.
observations.subgroup: US adults, adults under 30, influencer-news users, and published civic-engagement groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A person may use social news without being persuaded, or participate civically because of pre-existing identity or institutions rather than platform exposure.

observations.period: September 11, 2025; FTC AI companion inquiry launch

information_domains_requested.value: monetization, data use, safety testing, age limits, disclosures, and effects on children and teens

observations.method: FTC institutional action record; the inquiry requested information from companies and did not itself adjudicate harm.
observations.uncertainty: An inquiry establishes scrutiny and information demand, not verified injury, unlawful conduct, causation, remedy, or successful exit.
observations.subgroup: Consumer-facing AI companion users, with children and teens named as a risk focus.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional attention may produce learning and safeguards without establishing that the underlying product effects are widespread or severe.

related_sources.claim: FTC inquiry materials define the institutional information-gathering context and requested risk domains.
Pew adult AI findings provide the current use, purpose, privacy, and governance comparison.

boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled cross-source record. It establishes distinct reach, use, purpose, attention, civic, and institutional-scrutiny signals, but does not establish a common digital exposure, platform causation, dependence, privacy loss, political persuasion, consumer spending effect, harm, remedy, or exit cost. A linked respondent panel, product telemetry, terms/data audit, complaint and remedy records, and longitudinal switching outcomes are still required to test the end-to-end mechanism.
